notes: M2.9L suffix-lookup drafts (tasks/m29l-spec.md D6/D7): the native-g0-qwen38-flash-next-v10 speculation profile on a library that also verifies suffix-lookup drafts. It ships spec_drafts mtp (MTP drafts only) because M1 gave ship-mtp: combined was not faster than MTP-only beyond noise on the agent workload. With spec_drafts mtp+lookup, set per config, each round drafts from the MTP head or from a suffix match in the session's own context, as the request's draft policy chooses. The VERIFY path is unchanged, so outputs stay bit-identical to plain greedy (lossless). MTP/NEXTN speculative decoding (tasks/m29-spec.md D11/D12, OQ8): the shipped native-g0-qwen38-flash-next-v8 profile with speculative_draft_tokens 4 (the artifact's MTP draft on DEVICE, chain 3/1/4), bit-identical to plain greedy (K4/R3): every round verifies the session's pending drafts as consecutive decode rows of the plain kernel sequence and commits the target's tokens, so tokens and scores equal the plain run. Verify rows mirror unconstrained decode only (text and tool_calls, greedy and sampled); constrained, ignore_eos, min_tokens, penalty, logit_bias and image tickets never speculate (NO_SPECULATION). Otherwise as the shipped profile: Deterministic at rows = 1 without cache (K8/X11 repeat evidence); NVFP4 W4A4 and fp8_e4m3 KV; MoE scales as flashinfer_cutlass (Q14), N experts with up != gate scale. The in-process CERE executor (libcere_executor.so, ABI v4) on GPU0: up to 4 rows, text in and out (tool calls parsed by CERE as SGLang's qwen3_coder detector; stop strings matched by CERE), no prefix cache. Rows are concurrently decoded sessions in one batched decode step, bit-identical to each session decoded as one row (M2.6 C/K evidence); prefill is serialized, one 4,096-token chunk of one session per round, alternating with decode rounds (prefill row_counts [1]). Greedy decoding (temperature < 1e-6 or top_k 1 with neutral processors) runs the unchanged greedy path; sampled decoding (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, seed, frequency/presence/repetition penalties, logit_bias) and logprobs with top_logprobs up to 20 run the M2.7 device sampler, which the library must report (native_sampler 1, checked at start). Each row of a batched decode step samples with its own sampling, output counts and counter key (its session position; ledger CR4), so a sampled session commits the same tokens at rows 1-4 whatever else shares the round. The sampler is checked against its own logits and its CPU reference only: it is not an SGLang parity claim (G1 has not passed), and seeded outputs are reproducible on this artifact and library, not SGLang's sequence. n > 1 runs n sessions as rows (n <= 4, no session turn or continue mode); sampled choice i >= 1 draws with a distinct per-choice seed (ledger M8 channels (2, 3)). Grammar (M2.8): response_format json_object/json_schema (dialect json-schema-2020-12/xgrammar-0.2.1, the listed keywords only; numeric bounds only on integer schemas in enforced forms), top-level regex and ebnf, and tool_choice required/named or a strict tool (tool_calls_constrained) are enforced in the executor: the grammar process (xgrammar 0.2.1, sidecar --role grammar) supplies per-position vocab masks, which the library must accept (native_token_mask 1, checked at start), and the executor masks the scored row after penalties and before logit_bias (K12, SGLang order); a constrained row waits for its mask each decode round (ledger CR5) and constrained tickets never speculate (I3); one constraint per request, greedy or sampled, rows as text decoding; outputs are not post-validated, and this is not a throughput claim. snapshot/restore, images and prompts over the context limit are absent and therefore refused. Not a throughput or capacity claim.
